title: Is Anything Too Hard for the Lord?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the Lord said to Abraham, "Why did Sarah laugh and say, 'Will I really have a child, now that I am old?' Is anything too hard for the Lord? I will return to you at the appointed time next year, and Sarah will have a son." - Gen 18:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the greatest questions in all of Scripture: "Is anything too hard for the Lord?" God gently confronts Sarah's disbelief, not with a rebuke, but with a question that reframes everything. The issue was never Sarah's age or worn-out body. The issue was whether anything at all could be too hard for the God who made the universe.

Sit with that question. Is anything too hard for the Lord? The God who spoke galaxies into being, who parted seas and raised the dead - is a barren womb too much for Him? Is your impossible situation too much for Him? The question answers itself. Nothing is too hard for the Lord.

Notice that God overheard Sarah's private laugh, even her silent thoughts. "Why did Sarah laugh?" He knew what she had said only "to herself." God knows our secret doubts, the quiet unbelief we hide even from those around us. And He addresses them - not to shame us, but to lift our eyes to His power.

This question echoes through the whole Bible. The angel told Mary, "For no word from God will ever fail" (Luke 1:37). Jesus said, "What is impossible with man is possible with God" (Luke 18:27). Whatever impossibility you face today - in your body, your family, your circumstances - bring it under this question. Is this too hard for the Lord? It is not.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What impossibility are you facing that you need to bring under this question?
- Do you believe nothing is too hard for the Lord?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Almighty God, nothing is too hard for You. When I face the impossible, remind me who You are. You know my secret doubts, and You lift my eyes to Your power. I bring my impossibility to You today.
Amen.
